name: Wankhede Stadium
notes: High-scoring venue. Dew heavily favors chasing teams after over 30. Short square boundaries amplify power hitting. Sea breeze in evening sessions helps pace bowlers early.

name: Eden Gardens
notes: Spin-friendly surface that turns from day one in Test matches. Massive crowd atmosphere creates pressure. Significant dew plays a big role in day-night games — chasing teams benefit greatly.

name: M. A. Chidambaram Stadium
notes: Notorious spin paradise. Off-spinners and leg-spinners dominate from day one. Extreme heat and humidity affects pace bowlers. Low-scoring in Tests due to turn and variable bounce.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
notes: World's largest cricket stadium. Flat batting surface in limited overs. Spin effective in Tests. Day-night matches see some dew but large outfield reduces boundary count.

name: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium
notes: Highest-scoring T20 ground in India. Very small boundaries and flat pitch. High altitude in Bangalore means ball travels further — premium on big hitters. Dew minimal due to cooler evenings.

name: Arun Jaitley Stadium
notes: Historically spin-friendly with variable bounce. Pollution and smog can affect visibility in evening games. Turns more as match progresses. Delhi winters make morning sessions tricky for batters.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
notes: Large boundaries significantly reduce scoring. Pace bowlers dominate with bounce and carry. Defending scores is easier here. Boxing Day Test is iconic — pitch hard and bouncy early, flattens by day 3.

name: Sydney Cricket Ground
notes: Unique drop-in pitch that can take significant spin in later days of Test matches. Historic venue with strong traditions. Smaller than MCG so more runs. SCG Test known for spin late in match.

name: The Gabba
notes: The Fortress — Australia traditionally won almost every Test here for 30+ years. Pace and bounce. Humid conditions help swing. First session on day 1 is critical. Not a high T20 scoring venue.

name: Perth Stadium (Optus)
notes: Fastest pitch in Australia. Pace and extra bounce. Extreme heat in Perth makes afternoon sessions tough for batters. True pace bowler's paradise. New stadium keeps legacy of WACA pace.

name: Lord's Cricket Ground
notes: Famous slope from Pavilion End to Nursery End assists right-arm pace significantly. Overcast English conditions increase swing. Home of cricket — massive historical significance. No floodlights so all day games.

name: Headingley
notes: Swing-friendly venue especially in overcast Leeds conditions. Smaller boundaries make it good for scoring. Pitch can be unpredictable. Site of famous Botham's Ashes and Ben Stokes' 2019 World Cup heroics.

name: Edgbaston
notes: Intimidating home crowd for England. Good batting surface with some assistance for pace in overcast. Spin can be effective in dry conditions. Strong fortress for England in all formats.

name: Gaddafi Stadium
notes: Spin-friendly surface in Tests. High dew factor in evening games affects T20s significantly. Home support creates fortress atmosphere. Pace bowlers can use new ball but spin dominates as match progresses.

name: National Stadium
notes: Sea-level pitch tends to be flat for batting. Dew affects night games significantly near the coast. Humidity helps swing in morning sessions. Good cricket surface but heavily influenced by dew after sundown.

name: Newlands
notes: Mountain backdrop behind the ground. Consistent swing and seam movement. Pace bowlers thrive all day. Cool Cape Town breeze aids conditions. Defending scores here — one of most bowler-friendly venues globally.

name: The Wanderers Stadium
notes: Highest altitude major cricket venue. Ball travels significantly further at 1748m above sea level. One of the highest-scoring ODI venues — 438 vs 434 record here. Flat pitch plus altitude equals batting paradise.

name: Kensington Oval
notes: Premier cricket ground in the Caribbean. Sea breeze assists pace bowling. Pitch has pace and bounce early. Humidity can swing ball. Caribbean atmosphere with lively crowd. Home venue for historic WI teams.

name: Sabina Park
notes: Fastest pitch in the Caribbean. Produced some of the most terrifying fast bowling displays in history. Pace and extra bounce — spinners rarely effective here. Hot humid conditions.

name: R. Premadasa Stadium
notes: Slow, turning track especially beneficial for spinners. High humidity and dew heavily favor chasing teams in T20s. Good batting surface early but deteriorates significantly. Crowd creates electric atmosphere.

name: Dubai International Stadium
notes: Spin is king on this slow low surface. Hard to score quickly — strokeplay difficult. Chasing teams benefit from dew after sundown. PSL and IPL-neutral venue. Large outfield reduces boundary count.

name: Sharjah Cricket Stadium
notes: Historic neutral venue — Afghanistan's adopted home. Very small ground makes it high-scoring despite slow pitch. Spinners dominate. Evening dew helps chasers. Partisan Afghan crowd when they play here.

name: Eden Park
notes: Smallest international cricket boundaries in the world — sixes commonplace. Rugby ground converted for cricket creates unusual dimensions. Pace gets movement. NZ's rugby culture creates unique atmosphere.

name: Basin Reserve
notes: Most wind-affected venue in international cricket — The Windy City. Pace bowlers love conditions here. Ball moves prodigiously in overhead conditions. Considered a challenge for all batters. No floodlights — daytime Tests only.

name: Shere Bangla National Stadium
notes: Extreme dew makes evening T20 chasing almost automatic — toss critical. Spin-friendly surface especially in Tests. Humidity affects swing bowling. Home advantage is significant due to conditions difficult for touring teams.

name: Harare Sports Club
notes: High altitude (1480m) means ball travels further. Generally flat pitch good for batting. Both pace and spin can be effective. Outfield is slow so boundaries harder to reach despite altitude. Intimate atmosphere.
